title: Transition-metal-loaded TiO 2  catalysts for CO oxidation: metal-dependent activity and surface redox properties
content: In this work, a series of M/TiO2 catalysts (M = Fe, Co, Ni, Cu and Zn) were prepared on the same TiO2 support under consistent impregnation, evaporation and calcination conditions to systematically compare the effects of metal identity on low-temperature CO oxidation. The thermal catalytic activity among the M/TiO2 catalysts followed the order Cu/TiO2 > Fe/TiO2 > Co/TiO2 > Ni/TiO2 > Zn/TiO2. Cu/TiO2 exhibited the highest activity, which was associated with its favorable low-temperature reducibility, mixed Cu oxidation states, and relatively high proportion of surface adsorbed or defect-related oxygen species. Light-assisted tests showed enhanced CO oxidation over Cu/TiO2, with the T10, T50 and T90 decreasing from 117, 158 and 180 °C under thermal conditions to 70, 77 and 100 °C under photothermal conditions, respectively. Meanwhile, the apparent activation energy decreased from 41.7 to 30.3 kJ mol−1. In situ DRIFTS under thermal conditions revealed that formate, carboxylate and carbonate species were important surface intermediates in the CO oxidation process over Cu/TiO2. After gaseous O2 was removed, these surface species continued to evolve, indicating that oxygen species retained on the catalyst surface could still participate in CO conversion. After O2 was reintroduced, the accumulated surface intermediates were further oxidized and the reaction gradually returned to equilibrium. These results indicated that surface oxygen species participated in the conversion of adsorbed CO, while gaseous O2 continuously replenished reactive oxygen species on the catalyst surface.
